rules.title: Jersey City Rent Control Ordinance (Chapter 260)
rules.requirement: Jersey City regulates rents through its Rent Control Ordinance, Chapter 260 of the Municipal Code. The Office of Landlord/Tenant Relations administers it. Landlords apply for rent increases (capital improvement, vacancy capital improvement, hardship) and tenants may petition over illegal rent or failure to maintain service. Properties with 1-4 units are exempt. The page does not give the cap formula.

unverifiable_exemptions: Other exemptions that an owner may request from the Office, which reviews them against the ordinance's permitted exemption criteria
coverage.summary: Applies to rental properties with 5 or more units; 1-4 unit properties are exempt.
coverage.other_conditions: Further exemptions are available on request if the owner meets the criteria for a permitted exemption.

rules.exemptions: All 1-4 unit properties are exempt; owners can submit a Rent Control Exemption Request for other permitted exemptions.
rules.effective_date_note: The page gives no effective date for the ordinance.
rules.quoted_span: All 1-4 Unit Properties are exempt from rent control
rules.review_note: This is an official city page summarizing the ordinance. It gives no cap percentage or CPI formula, so check the ordinance text itself.

result.doc_summary: Official Jersey City Office of Landlord/Tenant Relations page. It says the office administers Rent Control Ordinance Chapter 260 and notes that 1-4 unit properties are exempt. It also covers landlord registration, rent-increase applications through the Tyler portal, tenant petitions, a state liability-insurance requirement, and an adjourned Rent Leveling Board meeting. It has no text on just-cause eviction, deposits, screening or algorithmic rent-setting.
